source: Hand-checked pillar tags for task T1, read directly against each investigation's own NASA objective, hypothesis and research-impact text (data/raw/investigations/PSI-*.json), not just its title. First pass drafted by Claude at Mufeed's request so Taha reviews rather than starts from a blank file. Entries whose note starts with REVIEW disagree with the seed tags in docs/EXECUTION_PLAN.md section 8 and should get a second pair of eyes before judging day; everything else either matches the seed tags or corrects the model's extraction where the actual NASA text didn't support it. Taha: once you've checked these, feel free to edit this file directly and drop the REVIEW notes you've confirmed. Second pass on 15 Nov resolved the seven REVIEW entries against the same NASA objective and research-impact text, with the reason in each note. Taha has not reviewed them yet.

investigations.note: Soot-inception and extinction limits for gaseous diffusion flames, but the investigation's own stated impact is terrestrial power-plant combustors, not spacecraft safety. Kept prevention only; rejected the model's added suppression, no suppressant agent is tested here, only flame physics.

Upgraded from prevention-only. Objective tests NASA's actual candidate cabin atmospheres (14.7/21%, 10.2/26.5%, 8.2/34% O2), and the investigation's own impact text states cutting ventilation is an established step in putting out spacecraft fires and that unventilated burning persisted at elevated O2, both prevention and suppression relevant.

Pure coflow diffusion flame benchmark data for validating computational models. No NASA atmosphere context, no operational framing. Kept as seed had it; rejected the model's prevention/suppression tag as overreach.
The investigation's own impact text says plainly it is not conducted to serve any space application. Kept as seed had it; rejected the model's prevention tag.
Transient flame structure study for computational model comparison, impacts framed around terrestrial combustion devices. Kept as seed had it; rejected the model's prevention tag.
Objective explicitly ties results to fire detection and suppression system design and to bridging NASA's flammability test standard with real microgravity behavior. Seed and model agree here.
Objective explicitly tests an inert gaseous extinguishing agent (suppression) and flammability/material screening (prevention). Seed and model agree here.

Droplet cool-flame chemistry and extinction diameters, impact text framed around fuel and engine design broadly, not spacecraft safety. Kept prevention only (as seed); rejected the model's added suppression, no suppressant agent is tested.
Validates a particulate counter's reliability in microgravity, explicitly to support fire and smoke detection systems. Seed and model agree here.

Second pass 15 Nov: detection restored. The investigation's own research-impact text says the results support safer fire detection, and soot is what smoke detectors sense. Prevention kept for soot-formation understanding. Suppression not added: the same sentence names it, but no suppressant is studied.

Flame-spread modeling explicitly intended as a screening tool for new materials' flammability limits, to design safer spacecraft and manage fire risk. Kept seed's prevention tag; the model's call of zero pillars looks like an extraction miss, the text is clearly prevention relevant.
Second pass 15 Nov: kept prevention and suppression, consistent with FLEX on the same hardware. Its extinction boundaries over 10 to 40% oxygen bear on both.

Objective explicitly both maps flammability limits (prevention) and measures the effectiveness of CO2, He and SF6 suppressants (suppression). Upgraded from seed's suppression-only; matches the model here.

Second pass 15 Nov: prevention only. The objective is fire growth and low-g flammability limits. The O2 and CO2 sensors observe the fire; detection is not studied. Platform set to Cygnus: PSI's catalog lists ISS, but NASA's approach text says the burn ran on the Cygnus resupply vehicle after it left the station, the same as SAFFIRE-II.

Same objective text as SAFFIRE-I and III (fire growth rate and flammability limits). Kept prevention only for consistency across the three SAFFIRE missions; rejected the model's added suppression, no suppressant is tested, the fires are observed, not extinguished.

Second pass 15 Nov: prevention only, same objective text and instruments as SAFFIRE-I. Platform set to Cygnus: PSI's catalog lists ISS, but NASA's approach text says the burn ran on the Cygnus resupply vehicle after it left the station, the same as SAFFIRE-II.
Explicitly about smoke particle size for designing and evaluating spacecraft smoke detectors. Seed and model agree here.
Same as SAME-R: explicitly about smoke detector sensitivity to microgravity smoke. Seed and model agree here.

Laminar diffusion flame structure and liftoff study, impacts framed around terrestrial engine efficiency with one generic fire-safety mention. Kept as seed had it; rejected the model's prevention/detection tag.
Second pass 15 Nov: prevention only. Its impact text is about soot formation and safer spacecraft environments and does not mention detection. Smoke point is a fuel sootiness property.
Second pass 15 Nov: kept both. Its impact text says the models would lead to better smoke detection devices and prevent fires.
Second pass 15 Nov: prevention. Its stated space benefit is defining safer operating envelopes from cool-flame extinction behaviour.

Explicitly develops a flammability-limit diagram for cool flames and verifies it against the ISS FLEX results. Kept prevention only (as seed); rejected the model's added suppression, no suppressant agent is tested.

Cool diffusion flame conditions at elevated oxygen for gaseous fuels, directly relevant to spacecraft cabin flammability margins at high O2. Kept prevention only (as seed); rejected the model's added suppression, no suppressant agent is tested.
